scenario: Aug 12: The latest reviewed Al Jazeera report (Aug 11) records Hormuz crossings collapsing from 15 Friday to 6 Sunday while Iran and Oman have agreed coordinates for a temporary route, but no signed full reopening is confirmed. Trump continues to demand compensation from Iran and claim '100%' US control of the waterway (Al Jazeera/CNBC, Aug 11). Brent $89.11, WTI $83.47 and TTF 60.18 EUR/MWh; the JKM CFD reference remains $21.26 (Trading Economics, Aug 10) while the $22.00 September-delivery assessment remains carried. Qatar LNG force majeure remains carried through mid-September. Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 10%, stress 55%, tail 35%.

categories.label: Food & Agriculture
categories.supplyChainImpact: Middle East fertilizer and energy exports remain constrained while Hormuz traffic has fallen further to just 6 confirmed crossings on Sunday, down from 15 Friday and far below the ~88/day pre-war norm (MarineTraffic via Al Jazeera, Aug 11). Trump's Aug 11 demand that Iran pay '50 years' of reparations, layered on Iran's Aug 8 demands for a blockade end and sanctions relief, dims near-term reopening hopes, sustaining freight and input-cost risk for Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia planting chains, while Qatar force majeure remains extended to mid-September.

categories.label: Petrochemicals & Plastics
categories.supplyChainImpact: SABIC, QAPCO and Omani exporters depend on Gulf shipping, while Southeast Asian crackers rely on Gulf condensate and naphtha. Hormuz traffic fell further to just 6 crossings Sunday, down from 15 Friday (MarineTraffic via Al Jazeera, Aug 11), and Trump's Aug 11 demand for Iranian reparations - layered on Iran's own compensation and sanctions-relief demands - keeps the standoff unresolved, sustaining combined feedstock, freight and delivery risk for plastics, packaging and agrochemicals.

categories.label: Fertilizers
categories.supplyChainImpact: The Strait of Hormuz remains the critical export artery for Middle East fertilizer supply. Qatar force majeure is extended to mid-September, and Hormuz traffic fell further to just 6 crossings Sunday, down from 15 Friday, after Trump demanded Iran pay '50 years' of reparations and claimed '100%' US Navy control of Hormuz (MarineTraffic via Al Jazeera/CNBC, Aug 11). Urea, DAP and potash delivery risk therefore stays elevated across ASEAN planting chains pending a signed reopening.
